preconditions.description: The input is a single string of lowercase Latin letters with length between 1 and 100,000.

postconditions.description: The first line of output is an integer k representing the number of non-empty parts, which must be at least 1.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= len(stdin) and l > 0 for x, l in parts)
postconditions.description: Each part is defined by a 1-based start index x and a positive length l.

postconditions.expression: all(parts[i][0] < parts[i+1][0] for i in range(len(parts)-1))
postconditions.description: The parts are output in strictly increasing order of their start indices.

postconditions.expression: len(parts) == 1 or (len(parts) == 3 and parts[0][1] == parts[2][1] and parts[1][1] % 2 == 1)
postconditions.description: The solution consists of either 1 part (the whole password) or 3 parts (prefix, middle, suffix) where prefix and suffix have equal length and the middle part has odd length.

postconditions.expression: len(parts) == 1 or (parts[0][0] + parts[0][1] == parts[1][0] and parts[1][0] + parts[1][1] == parts[2][0])
postconditions.description: If there are 3 parts, they must be contiguous in the input string, forming a single substring.
If there are 3 parts, the prefix substring must be identical to the suffix substring.
If there are 3 parts, the middle substring must be a palindrome.
The concatenation of the three parts (prefix + middle + suffix) must form a palindrome.

postconditions.expression: total_len := sum(l for _, l in parts); all(total_len >= sum(l for _, l in alt_parts) for alt_parts in valid_solutions)
postconditions.description: The sum of lengths of the selected parts is maximized among all valid solutions.
